name: Tasman Front
scope: Historical Tasman Front naming convention represented by an OSW offshore 154 E to 172 E near-34 S regional connection. Gates truncate the Australia-northern-New-Zealand geography; neither coastal endpoints nor a continuously identifiable jet is claimed. Excludes coastal EAC, southern extension and East Auckland coastal continuation.
layer: Historical upper-ocean thermal/front circulation context, not a fixed-depth velocity core. No temperature contour or measured meander digitized.
time_convention: Undated historical reference connection. The source discusses separate September-October 1979 hydrography and March 1982-April 1985 SST statistics; neither supplies this drawn route. Later Oke et al. (2019) disputes a commonly continuous zonal jet.
source_locator: Chapter 8, printed pp127-129 / PDF137-139: Australia-New Zealand connection near 34 S, meanders and statistically defined average position. Version 1.1 March 2005. Cited pages and Figure 8.23 visually inspected.
source_citation: Tomczak, M. and J.S. Godfrey, Regional Oceanography: An Introduction (1994), university-hosted online compilation, chapter versions stated separately.
source_license: No redistribution license established; original retained locally and ignored. Paraphrased factual annotations and independent OSW vertices only; no original image or curve copied.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects offshore regional gates and rounded vertices within the described geography. Alternative shapes shift intermediate latitudes by +/- 0.5 degree; longitude and independent endpoint-latitude shifts test drawing convention. These choices are not measured current boundaries, physical uncertainty or seasonal extrema.

alternative_routes.interpretation: Alternative editorial shape between selected regional gates, not an observed axis or seasonal state.

scenario_rule: Three declared shapes crossed with three uniform longitude shifts and independent three-value endpoint latitude shifts: 81 retained editorial scenarios, not confidence limits or seasonal ranges.
remaining_gates: Independently review identity, layer, selected gates and fine coastline/bathymetry before physical admission.

Whole-current length, physical width and annual ranges remain unresolved.

supporting_sources.label: Oke et al. (2019), A search for the Tasman Front, doi:10.1016/j.jmarsys.2019.103217
supporting_sources.access: Abstract read; full 2019 article not acquired. Original temperature-data reinterpretation, reanalysis and drifters suggest discontinuous streams/eddy field; continuous zonal flow less common than conceptual models imply.

method: Sum shortest WGS84 geodesic distances between successive OSW editorial vertices; no velocity field or current core is reconstructed.
map_land_check: All 81 routes, geodesically densified at spacing no greater than 10 km, avoid the coarse OSW atlas land mask in display coordinates. This is not a shelf-break, reef, bathymetric or high-resolution land-clearance verification.
state_relation_role: Editorial line/display-region crossing; physical current passage unresolved.
